name: Catholicity
overview: Scripture reveals the catholicity of the Gospel as inclusive of all who fear God and practice righteousness, regardless of their background, as seen in Peter's recognition that God shows no partiality (Acts 10:34-35). Jesus' instruction to accept those who are not against His followers, even if they do not follow with them, highlights the unity and breadth of the Gospel mission (Mark 9:38; Luke 9:49-50). The example of Cornelius, a devout Gentile centurion, further illustrates the expanding reach of salvation beyond Israel (Acts 10:1). This catholicity is reflected in the early church’s openness, including the rulers at Antioch permitting the apostles to preach broadly.
